correctness.rationale: The moving-person utility inequalities use the destination degree, and the exact six-edge construction has before scores (0,1/3,1/2,0,2/3) and after scores (1,1/3,0,1/3,1/3). The A mover improves 0 to 1/3 and the B mover 2/3 to 1, whereas the count with own-type neighbor fraction at least 1/2 falls from 2 to 1. A self-contained standard-library exact checker enumerates every labeled graph through five vertices, canonicalizes its connected graph isomorphism classes by all permutations, visits each allowed two-color assignment, and tests each opposite-color swap. It verifies connected counts 1,4,38,728 and connected isomorphism classes 1,2,6,21 at n=2,3,4,5; precisely two five-vertex classes, with 6 and 7 edges, admit loss. The complete finite proof is independent of floating point. A separate graph-atlas class enumeration confirms the number and edge sizes of witness classes; no assertion on larger orders is made.

originality.rationale: The precise one-swap monotonicity obstruction for a binary half-neighbor satisfaction headcount is not a direct corollary of potential convergence or aggregate continuous utility. The relevant untruncated swap-game primary literature defines the moves but studies stability and overall welfare. Truncated-tolerance utility papers use a distinct player incentive; Zhang studies a different spatial utility. The published primary comparisons and searches did not reveal the sharp five-node threshold or two graph classes, while uninspected appendices and alternate sociophysics terminology remain residual risks.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent sharp small-graph example may exist in an uninspected appendix or other Schelling-game paper, including variants named integration welfare, tolerance welfare, or segregation potential.

Zhang (2011) publicly accessible bibliographic and abstract material was inspected but full paper was not accessible; its different preference model makes direct coverage less likely, but not impossible.
Finite correctness was checked with standalone exact code and one independent graph-atlas enumeration, not independently audited by a separate mathematical reviewer.

value.rationale: The number of agents with at least half their neighbors of the same type is a standard interpretable tolerance-based societal measure. Showing that two privately utility-improving swaps can make fewer people satisfied, even while the sum of continuous utilities rises, pinpoints a genuine aggregation failure rather than a generic downside in a changing graph. A sharp five-person boundary and the classification of both graph topologies specify exactly the first structural obstruction. The small finite threshold is motivated by the canonical Schelling move and common 50% satisfaction criterion; no claim of paper-sized downstream result is required.
